name: Maguro
alt: A reddish-pink slice of raw fish draped over a small mound of rice.
facts: This deep red fish is one of the most popular sushi fish in the whole world.
It can swim in fast bursts, which is part of why it's prized for its firm, meaty texture.

name: Sake
alt: A bright orange-pink slice of raw fish on top of a small mound of rice.
facts: This is the single most popular fish used in sushi in the United States.
Its bright orange color comes partly from the tiny shrimp-like creatures it eats in the wild.

name: Hamachi
alt: A pale, glossy slice of raw white fish over a mound of rice.
facts: This fish is named for a yellow stripe that runs along its side.
Chefs prize it for a buttery, mild flavor that's milder than redder sushi fish.

name: Ebi
alt: A curled, pink-and-white cooked shellfish draped over a mound of rice.
facts: This topping is cooked first, then split open and laid flat over the rice.
Its curled shape and pink-and-white stripes make it easy to spot on a sushi plate.

name: Unagi
alt: A glossy, dark-brown grilled topping glazed with sauce, laid over rice.
facts: This topping is grilled and brushed with a sweet, sticky sauce before serving.
Unlike most sushi toppings, it's never served raw.

name: Tako
alt: A pale, bumpy-textured slice with a reddish-purple edge draped over rice.
facts: This topping is boiled until tender, which turns its edge from gray to a reddish-purple.
Its bumpy texture comes from rows of tiny suckers.

name: Ika
alt: A smooth, milky-white slice with fine crisscross markings over a mound of rice.
facts: Chefs score this topping with tiny crisscross cuts so it's easier to chew.
It has a mild flavor and a slightly chewy, springy texture.

name: Hotate
alt: A round, pale ivory-colored piece of shellfish resting on a mound of rice.
facts: This topping comes from a shellfish that can actually swim by clapping its shell open and shut.
It has a naturally sweet taste and a soft, tender bite.

name: Ikura
alt: A small cup of rice wrapped in seaweed and piled high with glistening orange eggs.
facts: This topping is made of hundreds of tiny, glistening orange eggs.
Each little egg pops gently when you bite into it.

name: Uni
alt: A soft, golden-yellow, custard-like topping piled in a small seaweed-wrapped cup of rice.
facts: This topping comes from a spiky sea creature and has a soft, custardy texture.
Its color can range from pale yellow to deep orange depending on where it's harvested.
